cases.question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.standalone_question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture is a 3.0-credit course that focuses on the design, development, and management of web APIs. It is part of the Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma program.

The course covers the following key areas:
*   **RESTful APIs:** Understanding what they are, why they are important, and how they relate to HTTP.
*   **Core Concepts:** Exploring REST constraints, CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations, and the use of HTTP status codes.
*   **Practical Skills:** Designing and developing web services, documenting specifications, implementing error handling, and securing backend API servers.
*   **Management:** Applying versioning and change management to API designs.

Students are expected to use tools such as Visual Studio Code or IntelliJ IDEA and will work with technologies like Node.js, Express, and JSON. The course emphasizes interactive learning, including in-class activities, quizzes, assignments, and a group project. Please note that students are responsible for securing their own hosting for web applications and assignments throughout the term.

The prerequisites for this course are COMP 1537 and COMP 3522.

Sources:
- https://www.bcit.ca/courses/internet-software-architecture-comp-4537/
- https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-technology-diploma-full-time-5500dipma/
- https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261088086/
sub_queries: COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture course description and topics

cases.question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.standalone_question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics covers the following three main topic areas:

*   **Boolean algebra and the design of logic circuits:** This includes concepts such as Boolean variables, operators, truth tables, canonical forms, and simplification using mathematical proofs and Karnaugh maps.
*   **Number systems and data representation:** This covers positional number systems and how various data types—including numbers, text, and graphics—are represented within a computer, as well as performing arithmetic operations in different bases (binary, octal, and hexadecimal).
*   **Functions, linear equations, vectors, and matrices:** This area focuses on solving systems of linear equations, performing matrix operations, and applying algebraic methods and determinants.

Sources:
https://www.bcit.ca/courses/applied-mathematics-comp-1113/
https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261048068/

cases.question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.standalone_question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.answer_excerpt:
You are automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan if you are a student in a program designated as full-time by BCIT that lasts at least 16 weeks. The fee for this plan is automatically included in your tuition upon registration.

Regarding your ability to opt out:

*   **Eligibility to Opt Out:** You have the option to opt out of the plan if you are already covered by comparable extended health and dental benefits.
*   **Deadline:** You must process your opt-out within 30 days from the start of your program. This can be done once per 12-month period.
*   **Consequences:** After the 30-day deadline, opt-outs cannot be processed. If you successfully opt out, you are no longer covered by the BCITSA plan.

If you are unsure about your eligibility or need to manage your enrollment, you can visit or contact the BCITSA Health & Dental Plan Office located in building SE2 on the Burnaby campus.

Sources:
- https://www.bcit.ca/admission/tuition-fees/full-time-studies/
- https://www.bcitsa.ca/student-services/health-dental/
- https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/medical-insurance/types-of-insurance/

cases.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?
cases.follow_up: What TOEFL iBT score does Category 2 require?
cases.standalone_question: What TOEFL iBT score does BCIT English proficiency Category 2 require?

prior_turns.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?

cases.answer_excerpt:
For Category 2 English Language Proficiency, the required TOEFL iBT score depends on when you are applying:

*   **Prior to January 21, 2026:** An overall score of 86 is required, with no section score less than 20.
*   **As of January 21, 2026:** An overall score of 4.5 is required, with a minimum score of 3.5 in each of the Speaking, Writing, Reading, and Listening sections.

Please note that test results must be dated no more than two years before your program start date.

Sources:
https://www.bcit.ca/admission/entrance-requirements/english-language-proficiency/
